results.title: SOP for Sample Handling, Transport, and Chain of Custody
results.content: The following steps should be followed for all types of samples prior to sample collection: (1) verify what, if any, field processing requirements are needed for the constituents to be analyzed, (2) collect and assemble equipment necessary for sample collection, handling and transport, (3) prepare documentation (COC, field sheets and logbooks) pertaining to sample collection, handling, and transport, (4) pre-label collection bottles and sample bottles, and (5) establish and maintain a clean working area. results.content: # What are laboratory standards and reference materials? Dr. Deepak August 4, 2017. Standards and reference materials play a crucial role in any analysis. It is just not possible to imagine any analysis in which a standard reference is not involved. Identification of sample components can be made only against reference to a known standard. Similarly the amount of any component in the sample can be determined by comparison of observed response with the response obtained from unknown quantity of a standard in the same sample matrix and under identical experimental conditions. #### Standard. Standard is a material used to check the quality and metrological traceability of products, validate analytical methods or for calibration of analytical instruments. #### Reference Material. Reference material is a homogeneous and stable compound with respect to one or more specified properties which have been established for use in a measurement process. #### Certified Reference Material. Certified reference material is characterized by a valid procedure for one or more specified properties. #### Role of Standards in Calibration. Such laboratories rely heavily on certified reference materials. Measurement traceability relates to the value of a standard which can be associated with national or international standard bodies through an unbroken chain of comparison all having stated uncertainties. #### Types of Standard Reference Materials. **Reference materials can be sourced from globally recognized standard bodies such as NIST. Dr Deepak Bhanot is a seasoned professional having nearly 30 years expertise beginning from sales and product support of analytical instruments. ## Understand Laboratory Standards and Reference Materials. Analytical results can be relied upon only if they are related to standards and reference materials. Dr. Deepak May 11, 2016. 1. Dr. Deepak August 16, 2017. As certified reference materials are very expensive so for routine use working standards are prepared from high purity compounds and their active compound concentration is determined in comparison with CRM.As the working standard may deteriorate over time another one is prepared before ist retest or expiry date once again with reference to the CRM so in the process the traceability chain to original CRM is not broken.

results.title: Reference Materials Are Essential to Determine Uncertainty in Measurement for Spark Spectrometry - Analyzing Metals
results.content: / Reference Materials Are Essential to Determine Uncertainty in Measurement for Spark Spectrometry. # Reference Materials Are Essential to Determine Uncertainty in Measurement for Spark Spectrometry. Every measurement comes with uncertainty. This calculation of the uncertainty in measurement is where reference materials play a key role, especially in a field as specific as spark spectrometry. With spark spectrometry of metals knowledge of the level of uncertainty in measurement is hugely important, and is necessary to properly validate measurement results. According to DIN EN ISO 17025, the worldwide standard for laboratory accreditation in the area of testing and calibration, it is necessary to calculate the measurement uncertainty for each measurement result. ## Uncertainty in measurement for reference materials. [To put it in more technical terms, according to the Guide to the Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement (GUM) and the International Vocabulary of Metrology (VIM), the uncertainty of measurement is a measure of the dispersion of values that can reasonably be attributed to a measurement result. These known samples are called reference materials, and measurements of unknown samples can be compared to them. Uncertainty in measurement for reference materials needs to be accounted for and applied to measurements of unknowns. Four types of reference materials can be used for spark spectrometry: Setting Up samples, reference materials (RMs), Certified reference materials (CRMs), and Traceable CRMs. Setting up samples, such as RE12, do not have assigned concentration values for all elements in the certificate and do not provide information about measurement uncertainties. These samples cannot be used for calculating measurement uncertainties. CRMs provide average concentration values and the uncertainty of each element, as well as information about the method of preparation, sampling, chemical analysis, estimation of uncertainties, and traceability. CRM certificates also describe the details of production and certification according to relevant standards (such as ISO Guide 31, 35 and ISO 17034) and the Guide to the Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement (GUM) requirements. Regardless of the system operator or the sample preparation method, or what your exact application of spark OES spectrometry may be having the right reference materials for the job is essential to calculate the measurement uncertainty for each result and keep compliant with laboratory accreditation standards. results.title: Managing Reference Standards and Calibration Materials | Lab Manager
results.content: # Managing Reference Standards and Calibration Materials. The integrity of every result, from a simple pH reading to a complex quantitative analysis, hinges on the quality and handling of your foundational tools: reference standards and calibration materials. ## Foundational Principles of Reference Standards Management. A successful **reference standards management** program begins with a clear understanding of what these materials are and what they are not. * **Centralized Inventory and Tracking:** The first step is to create a single, centralized record for every reference standard and calibration material in your lab. * **Defined Use and Handling Protocols:** Your lab's Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) must clearly outline how each type of material is to be handled, prepared, and used. ## Best Practices for Reference Standards Lifecycle Management. Effective **reference standards management** is a continuous process that spans the entire lifecycle of the material, from the moment it arrives in your lab until its final disposition. A good **reference standards management** system will send automated alerts to remind you when a material is approaching its expiration date. ## Using Digital Solutions for Reference Standards Management. Modern labs are turning to digital solutions to streamline **reference standards management** and eliminate common pain points. By investing in a robust digital system, a lab not only improves its **reference standards management** but also elevates its overall data integrity and operational efficiency. ## Traceability and Uncertainty in Reference Standards Management. For every laboratory professional, the concepts of traceability and measurement uncertainty are intrinsically linked to effective **reference standards management**. Proper **reference standards management** is the mechanism by which your lab ensures both are upheld. ## Enhancing Lab Operations with Proactive Reference Standards Management. Effective **reference standards management** is more than a quality control task; it's a strategic imperative that underpins every aspect of a lab's performance. **What is the primary difference between a reference standard and a calibration material?**. While often used interchangeably, a reference standard (or Certified Reference Material) typically comes with a certificate of analysis and an established chain of traceability to a national or international standard, along with a stated uncertainty. **Can a small lab truly benefit from digital reference standards management software?**.
